2023_050_start_times_survey_report_3_2.paragraph: Presentation slides titled "School Start Time," prepared for a Troy Board of Education Workshop dated March 2, 2021 and carried in the April 4, 2023 board packet, reporting the results of a district-wide survey on moving high school start times later. Troy has operated a 5-tier bus schedule with a 7:20am high school start since 2011, a shift that reduced the bus fleet by 14 busses and cut transportation costs by about $800,000 per year. Survey responses came from 3,297 parents, 2,208 students and 878 staff. The deck's stated key finding is that between two-thirds and three-fourths of stakeholders say the District should follow the research and change the high school start time to later in the morning.
2023_050_start_times_survey_report_3_2.page:
**What this is**
Slide deck presented at a Troy Board of Education Workshop dated March 2, 2021 and included in the April 4, 2023 board packet as "Start Times Survey Report 3-2." Stated key takeaways (Slide 2): review of survey data, next steps, and timeline.

**Background (Slide 3)**
The Board had been studying high school start times for four years. When state funding was cut to its lowest point in 2011, the District moved from a 3-tier schedule (one start time each for elementary, middle and high schools) to a 5-tier bussing schedule. The change produced staggered start times for different elementary and middle school buildings, reduced the bus fleet by 14 busses, and reduced transportation costs by about $800,000 per year. To keep the latest-starting elementary buildings from releasing close to 5pm, high school start times were shifted earlier to 7:20am. The deck notes this burdened teens with early "get-ups" and made after-school teacher professional development and collaboration difficult because teachers of similar grades end their teaching day at different times. The District has operated on this schedule since 2011 to be as cost-efficient as possible.

**Research cited**
National studies show high schoolers' melatonin levels do not permit a healthy night's sleep when schools start before 8:00am, with 8:30am cited as closer to optimal. Associated outcomes listed: higher rates of tardiness, absenteeism and truancy; lower academic achievement across the entire school day, not only first hour; double-digit increases in teen driving accidents throughout the day and evening; higher rates of juvenile delinquency and arrest; and higher rates of teen depression and stress-related health disorders. Studies also show students in high schools that shift later do get more sleep. Both the Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the American Academy of Pediatrics recommend high schools start at least at 8:00am and ideally 8:30am or later.

**Arguments for keeping early starts (Slide 4)**
Cheaper bus routing; earlier high school starts let elementary and middle schools start later; earlier dismissal lets after-school activities start earlier (though Oakland County game times typically start after 4pm, so a later Troy end time would not affect them); students leave before parents depart for work and can be home to care for younger siblings.

**Survey samples**
| Group | Respondents |
|---|---|
| Parents | 3,297 |
| Students | 2,208 |
| Staff | 878 |

High-school-only cross-tabs used parent and student subgroups of 1,670 and 1,360 plus 321 staff. Parents-only breakouts: elementary 1,679, middle school 1,282, high school 1,670. Students-only: 5th graders 420, middle school 428, high school 1,360. Staff-only: elementary 390, middle school 217, high school 321.

**Reported results**
On the importance question, the three response options ("not a significant problem," "good to correct but can wait until school funding is better," and "a critical problem that needs to be corrected as soon as possible") drew 50%/45%/38%, 34%/35%/41% and 16%/20%/21% from parents, students and staff. The high-school-only version drew 51%/46%/36%, 30%/28%/31% and 18%/26%/32%. On the action question — keep the current 5-tier schedule with high schools at 7:20am, or increase the school budget assigned to bus service to move high school start times later — the split was 73%/66%/62% against 27%/34%/38%; the high-school-only version showed 62%/69%/54% against 38%/31%/46%.

**Key findings (Slide 14) and next steps (Slide 15)**
Between two-thirds and three-fourths of stakeholders say follow the research and change the high school start time to later in the morning; about 30% of each respondent group are willing to provide some leeway as to when the change is adopted; the traditional cadence (HS, MS, EL) is preferred. Next steps: Board questions, budget prioritization, and a decision point in early April.
2023_050_start_times_survey_report_3_2.verbose:
Slide deck titled "School Start Time," prepared for a Troy Board of Education Workshop dated March 2, 2021 and carried in the April 4, 2023 board packet under the title "Start Times Survey Report 3-2." Slide 2 lists the key takeaways as review of survey data, next steps, and timeline.

**History of the 5-tier schedule (Slide 3).** The deck states the Board of Education had been studying the topic for the past four years. When state funding was cut to its lowest point in 2011, the District made the decision to shift from a 3-tier schedule — one start time for elementary, one for middle schools, and one for high schools — to a 5-tier bussing schedule. That produced staggered start times for different elementary and middle school buildings but allowed the District to use busses more efficiently: the bus fleet was reduced by 14 busses and transportation costs fell by about $800,000 per year. The change was not without problems. To make sure the latest-starting elementary buildings did not end so late that children were arriving home close to 5pm, the District shifted high school start times earlier, to 7:20am. That put an added burden on teens in terms of early "get-ups" and made after-school teacher professional development and collaboration very difficult, because teachers of similar grades now end their teaching day at different times. The District has operated on this schedule since 2011, recognizing those negative impacts, in order to be as cost-efficient as possible.

**Research basis.** In the past five years a growing body of evidence suggests the decision to push high school start times to 7:20am may not be optimal for the social/emotional health or the academic achievement of Troy's high school students. Recent national studies show high schoolers' melatonin levels do not allow them to fall asleep early enough to capture a healthy night's sleep when schools start before 8:00am, and that high schools should ideally start closer to 8:30am for optimal sleep. National research associates consistent lack of sleep in early-start high schools with higher rates of tardiness, absenteeism and truancy; lower academic achievement, not only in first hour but across the entire school day; double-digit increases in teen driving accidents throughout the day and evening; higher rates of juvenile delinquency and arrest; and higher rates of teen depression and stress-related health disorders. Studies have also shown that students in high schools that shift to later start times do in fact get more sleep, countering a common argument that students will just stay up later. In light of those findings, both the Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the American Academy of Pediatrics recommend that high schools shift start times to at least 8:00am, and ideally to 8:30am or later. That recommendation prompted the Board of Education to begin studying a possible return to a 3-tier bus schedule so the District could shift high school start times to 8:00am or later.

**Why early high school start times persist (Slide 4).** Reasons listed: more efficient bus routing, timing and sharing that lowers district transportation costs; an earlier high school start time allows elementary and middle schools to start later; an earlier high school end time allows extracurricular and after-school activities to start earlier — although because high school game times across Oakland County typically start after 4pm, a later end time in Troy would not impact high school game times for Troy students; early-start high school students are more likely to leave for school in the morning before their parents leave for work; and early-start high school students can be home in time to receive younger siblings and provide after-school care for them.

**Survey participation.** The survey drew 3,297 parents, 2,208 students and 878 staff. On the question of which grades respondents have students enrolled in, are enrolled in, or teach — offering preschool, elementary, middle school, high school and post-secondary, with multiple responses allowed so totals add to more than 100% — the printed chart values are 4%, 62%, 19%, 44%, 39%, 19%, 25%, 51%, 62%, 37% and 3%. A footnote indicates the student sample at the elementary level consists of 5th graders only.

**Importance of moving high school start times later.** Respondents chose among "To me, this isn't a significant problem and probably doesn't need addressing," "This is something that would be good to correct, but we can wait to fix it until school funding is better at some point," and "This is a critical problem that needs to be corrected on as soon as possible." Across all parents (n=3,297), students (n=2,208) and staff (n=878), the printed shares are 50%, 45% and 38%; 34%, 35% and 41%; and 16%, 20% and 21%. A high-school-only version of the same question, with respondent counts of 1,360, 1,670 and 321, shows 51%, 46% and 36%; 30%, 28% and 31%; and 18%, 26% and 32%.

**Action preference.** Asked to weigh the research on teen sleep patterns and the negative impact of early high school start times against the additional bus service costs of a later high school start, respondents chose between keeping the current 5-tier bus schedule with staggered start times for different elementary and middle school buildings (high schools continuing to start at 7:20am) and increasing the amount of money in the school budget assigned to bus service so high school start times could move later in the morning. Across all parents, students and staff the printed shares are 73%, 66% and 62% against 27%, 34% and 38%. The high-school-only version shows 62%, 69% and 54% against 38%, 31% and 46%.

**3-tier schedule options.** If the District moved to a 3-tier bus schedule, six approximate start/end combinations were offered: Elementaries 8:00am to 2:58pm / Middle schools 8:30am to 3:14pm / High schools 9:00am to 3:50pm; Elementaries 8:00am to 2:58pm / High schools 8:30am to 3:20pm / Middle schools 9:00am to 3:44pm; Middle schools 8:00am to 2:44pm / Elementaries 8:30am to 3:28pm / High schools 9:00am to 3:50pm; Middle schools 8:00am to 2:44pm / High schools 8:30am to 3:20pm / Elementaries 9:00am to 3:58pm; High Schools 8:00am to 2:50pm / Elementaries 8:30am to 3:28pm / Middle schools 9:00am to 3:44pm; and High Schools 8:00am to 2:50pm / Middle schools 8:30am to 3:14pm / Elementaries 9:00am to 3:58pm. On the combined chart (parents n=3,297, students n=2,208, staff n=878) the printed option shares range from 7% to 44%. A parents-only chart, asking which set would be most ideal for the household over the rest of their children's time in Troy Schools, breaks parents out by elementary (n=1,679), middle school (n=1,282) and high school (n=1,670) children, with printed shares ranging from 3% to 48%. A students-only chart, asking which set would be best for everyone in the District, breaks out 5th graders (n=420), middle school (n=428) and high school (n=1,360) students, with printed shares ranging from 4% to 52%. A staff-only chart, asking which set would be best for the District as a whole, breaks out elementary (n=390), middle school (n=217) and high school (n=321) staff, with printed shares ranging from 2% to 56%.

**Key findings (Slide 14).** Between two-thirds and three-fourths of stakeholders say follow the research and change high school start time until later in the morning. About 30% of each respondent group are willing to provide some leeway as to when that change is adopted. The traditional cadence (HS, MS, EL) is preferred.

**Next steps and timeline (Slide 15).** Board questions; budget prioritization; decision point in early April.

2023_051_first_student_driver_count_marc.paragraph: Weekly bus-driver staffing tracker for the Troy School District, presented in the April 4, 2023 board packet as an Excel worksheet named "DSR," covering the weeks of November 15, 2021 through March 20, 2023. Each week is scored twice: against the District's operating 5-tier route structure and against a hypothetical 3-tier structure requiring 75 Troy routes, 4 Clawson routes and 10 standby drivers, for 85 drivers needed or 89 with Clawson. In the final week recorded, March 20, 2023, 65 drivers including standbys were on hand against 61 needed for the 5-tier plan, a surplus of 4, while the same staffing stood 20 short of the 3-tier requirement.
2023_051_first_student_driver_count_marc.page:
**Document type**
Excel workbook, single sheet "DSR," submitted by First Student and dated in the packet title as "March 23." Rows are weekly, from 2021-11-15 through 2023-03-20; trailing blank rows carry zeros.

**Columns**
A 5-Tier Analysis block (Troy 5-Tier Routes, Clawson Routes, Standby Drivers Needed, Total drivers needed, Total Drivers w/Clawson, Total Drivers Including Standbys, Drivers Short/Long (+/-), Drivers Short/Long w/Clawson); a parallel 3-Tier Analysis block with the same fields; and a recruiting/attrition block (Apps Received, Applicants Interviewed, Applicants Hired, Applicants on Hold, Employee Resignations, Employee Terminations, Medical Leave).

**Fixed route assumptions**
Troy 5-tier routes are 55 per week through 2022-07-25 and 53 from 2022-08-01 onward. Clawson routes are 4 and standby drivers needed are 8 in every 5-tier week, giving 63 total drivers needed (67 with Clawson) through July 2022 and 61 (65 with Clawson) afterward. The 3-tier block is constant across every week: 75 Troy routes, 4 Clawson routes, 10 standbys, 85 total drivers needed, 89 with Clawson.

**Staffing trajectory (selected weeks)**
| Week | Troy 5-tier routes | Drivers incl. standbys | 5-tier short/long | 5-tier w/Clawson | 3-tier short/long | 3-tier w/Clawson |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021-11-15 | 55 | 56 | -7 | -11 | -29 | -33 |
| 2022-02-28 | 55 | 50 | -13 | -17 | -35 | -39 |
| 2022-07-25 | 55 | 56 | -7 | -11 | -29 | -33 |
| 2022-08-01 | 53 | 56 | -5 | -9 | -29 | -33 |
| 2022-12-12 | 53 | 65 | 4 | 0 | -20 | -24 |
| 2023-03-20 | 53 | 65 | 4 | 0 | -20 | -24 |

Driver headcount bottomed at 50 in the week of 2022-02-28 and first reached parity with the 5-tier requirement in the week of 2022-08-29, when 61 drivers matched 61 needed. Staffing sat at 63 or 64 through most of January and February 2023 before returning to 65.

**Recruiting and attrition**
Weekly applications received range from 0 to 23, the peak being 2022-08-08 (23 received, 11 interviewed, 2 hired). Other heavy weeks include 2022-08-01 (14 received, 9 interviewed), 2022-07-18 (9 received, 9 interviewed, 1 hired), 2022-07-11 (10 received) and 2022-10-10 (8 received, 19 interviewed, 1 hired). Both 2023-03-06 and 2023-03-13 are recorded as zero across every recruiting and attrition field. The last row, 2023-03-20, shows 5 applications received, 1 hired, 0 on hold, 0 resignations, 0 terminations and 1 driver on medical leave.

Resignations appear in scattered single weeks, with 3 recorded in the weeks of 2021-12-06 and 2022-06-20. Terminations are recorded as 1 in the weeks of 2022-03-14, 2022-04-11 and 2023-01-02 and 2 in the week of 2022-09-19. Drivers on medical leave run at 2 through most of the 2021-22 school year, reach 4 in the weeks of 2022-05-09 through 2022-05-23, fall to 0 from 2022-08-15 through the end of February 2023, and stand at 1 in the final week.
2023_051_first_student_driver_count_marc.verbose:
Excel workbook submitted to the Troy Board of Education for the April 4, 2023 meeting, titled "First Student Driver Count March 23," containing a single sheet named "DSR" that tracks school bus driver supply week by week from 2021-11-15 through 2023-03-20. The sheet is built as two parallel analyses — a 5-Tier Analysis of the schedule the District actually operates and a 3-Tier Analysis of the alternative schedule under consideration in the concurrent school start time discussion — followed by a recruiting and attrition block.

**Column structure.** The 5-Tier Analysis block carries Troy 5-Tier Routes, Clawson Routes, Standby Drivers Needed, Total drivers needed, Total Drivers w/Clawson, Total Drivers Including Standbys, Drivers Short/Long (+/-), and Drivers Short/Long w/Clawson. The 3-Tier Analysis block repeats the same eight fields for Troy 3-Tier Routes. The final block records Apps Received, Applicants Interviewed, Applicants Hired, Applicants on Hold, Employee Resignations, Employee Terminations, and Medical Leave.

**Route and staffing requirements.** Troy 5-tier routes are entered as 55 for every week from 2021-11-15 through 2022-07-25 and as 53 for every week from 2022-08-01 through 2023-03-20. Clawson routes are 4 in every week and standby drivers needed are 8 in every week, yielding total drivers needed of 63 (67 with Clawson) in the 55-route weeks and 61 (65 with Clawson) in the 53-route weeks. The 3-Tier Analysis is held constant for the entire file: 75 Troy 3-tier routes, 4 Clawson routes, 10 standby drivers needed, 85 total drivers needed, and 89 total drivers with Clawson.

**Driver headcount over time.** The Total Drivers Including Standbys column opens at 56 on 2021-11-15, falls to 54 for the weeks of 2021-11-22 and 2021-11-29, and drops to 51 for the weeks of 2021-12-06, 2021-12-13, 2021-12-20, 2022-01-10 and 2022-01-17. It edges to 52 for 2022-01-24, 2022-01-31 and 2022-02-07, back to 51 for 2022-02-14 and 2022-02-21, and reaches its low of 50 in the week of 2022-02-28. Recovery follows: 51 on 2022-03-07, 52 on 2022-03-14, 54 on 2022-03-21 and 2022-03-28, 55 on 2022-04-04, 54 on 2022-04-11, 53 on 2022-04-18, 55 on 2022-04-25, 54 on 2022-05-02, 53 for the weeks of 2022-05-09, 2022-05-16 and 2022-05-23, then 56 on 2022-05-30 and 2022-06-06 and 57 on 2022-06-13. Summer weeks run 54 from 2022-06-20 through 2022-07-11, 55 on 2022-07-18, and 56 on 2022-07-25 and 2022-08-01. The count then climbs steadily through the fall: 57 on 2022-08-08, 58 on 2022-08-15, 59 on 2022-08-22, 61 on 2022-08-29, 62 on 2022-09-05 and 63 on 2022-09-12, before slipping to 60 for the weeks of 2022-09-19, 2022-09-26 and 2022-10-03. It returns to 61 on 2022-10-10 and 2022-10-17, 63 for 2022-10-24 through 2022-11-14, 62 on 2022-11-21 and 2022-11-28, 63 on 2022-12-05, 65 on 2022-12-12, and 63 on 2022-12-19. Calendar 2023 weeks read 62 on 2023-01-02, 63 on 2023-01-09, 2023-01-16 and 2023-01-23, 64 on 2023-01-30, 63 on 2023-02-06, and 64 for 2023-02-13, 2023-02-20, 2023-02-27, 2023-03-06 and 2023-03-13, closing at 65 on 2023-03-20.

**Shortfall against the two schedules.** Under the 5-tier structure the Drivers Short/Long column opens at -7 on 2021-11-15, deepens to -9, -12 and -13 across the winter of 2021-22 (worst at -13 in the week of 2022-02-28, or -17 counting Clawson), and improves through spring and summer to -5 on 2022-08-01. It reaches 0 in the weeks of 2022-08-29, 2022-10-10 and 2022-10-17, turns positive at +1 on 2022-09-05, and finishes at +2 and +3 through the winter before ending at +4 in the weeks of 2022-12-12 and 2023-03-20. Measured with Clawson routes included, the same weeks run from -11 at the start to 0 in the weeks of 2022-12-12 and 2023-03-20. Under the 3-tier structure the deficit is far larger and never closes: -29 on 2021-11-15, a worst reading of -35 in the week of 2022-02-28 (-39 with Clawson), -29 through the summer of 2022, and a best reading of -20 (-24 with Clawson) in the weeks of 2022-12-12 and 2023-03-20.

**Recruiting activity.** Applications received per week range from 0 to 23. The largest intake weeks are 2022-08-08 with 23 applications received, 11 applicants interviewed and 2 hired; 2022-08-01 with 14 received and 9 interviewed; 2022-08-15 with 10 received and 13 interviewed; 2022-07-11 with 10 received and 4 interviewed; 2022-09-12 with 10 received and 4 interviewed; and 2022-11-14 with 10 received, 3 interviewed and 1 hired. The week of 2022-10-10 records 8 applications received but 19 applicants interviewed and 1 hired. Weeks of 2023-03-06 and 2023-03-13 record 0 in every recruiting and attrition column. Applicants hired are recorded in single digits per week, most often 0, 1 or 2 — including 2 in the weeks of 2022-01-24, 2022-03-07, 2022-04-25, 2022-05-30, 2022-08-08, 2022-08-29, 2022-10-24 and 2022-12-12. Applicants on hold peak at 6 in the week of 2022-06-27.

**Attrition and leave.** Employee resignations are recorded as 1 on 2021-11-15, 3 on 2021-12-06, 1 on 2022-01-24, 1 on 2022-02-14, 1 on 2022-03-07, 1 on 2022-05-09, 3 on 2022-06-20, 1 on 2022-07-18, 1 on 2022-08-08, 1 on 2022-08-15, 1 on 2022-09-19, 1 on 2022-09-26, 1 on 2022-10-31, 1 on 2022-11-14, 1 on 2022-11-21, 2 on 2022-12-19 and 1 on 2023-02-06. Employee terminations are recorded as 1 in the weeks of 2022-03-14, 2022-04-11 and 2023-01-02 and as 2 in the week of 2022-09-19. Medical leave sits at 2 for most weeks from 2021-11-22 through the spring of 2022, rises to 3 in the weeks of 2022-02-28, 2022-03-07 and 2022-05-02, peaks at 4 in the weeks of 2022-05-09, 2022-05-16 and 2022-05-23, returns to 3 for the remaining June and July weeks, falls to 2 in early August, holds at 0 from 2022-08-15 through 2023-03-13, and shows 1 in the final row on 2023-03-20, which also records 5 applications received, a blank interview count, 1 applicant hired, and no applicants on hold, resignations or terminations.

The sheet ends with fifteen empty date rows carrying zeros in the computed total and short/long columns.

2023_052_2c_business_services_update.paragraph: Business Services presentation to the Troy Board of Education on April 4, 2023, covering Amendment 1 to the 2022-23 budgets for the District's three special revenue funds: Food Service, Community Service and Troy Preschool. All three are amended upward on the strength of federal money, with Food Service projecting a $535,000 surplus and a $2.6 million fund balance, Community Service a $1.5 million surplus and $2.5 million fund balance, and Preschool a $1.1 million surplus and $1.8 million fund balance. The deck closes with a budget calendar running from April through the audit of the 2022-23 financial statements in June through October.

2023_052_2c_business_services_update.verbose:
Business Services update delivered to the Troy Board of Education on April 4, 2023, presenting Amendment 1 to the 2022-23 budgets for the District's three special revenue funds. The deck defines each fund: the Food Service Fund accounts for revenue and expenses associated with the District's food service program; the Community Service Fund accounts for revenue and expenses associated with the District's fee-for-service programs, including CARE company and community recreation; and the Troy Preschool Fund accounts for revenue and expenses associated with the operation of the Troy School District Preschool program.

2023_053_vs_secondary.paragraph: Furniture quotation from VS America, Inc. to the Troy School District, Quote Number 0200149769, Revision 3, dated 03/17/2023 with an original quote date of 03/01/2023, presented to the Board on March 21, 2023. It equips eight secondary classrooms — four at Baker Middle School and four at International Academy East — with tables, stools, seating modules and storage priced at Omnia Partners Region 4 ESC contract net values under contract R191818, at a 22.40000% discount off list. The quotation totals $73,355.53, consisting of a $66,990.53 furniture subtotal plus $6,365.00 for installation.
